title: How the Internet Crosses the Oceans
summary: Almost all data between continents travels as light through about 550 thin cables on the seabed, coming ashore at a few beaches.

pages.section: Hook: your video from another continent goes under the sea, not through space
pages.say: When you open a website hosted in New York from London, how does the data cross the Atlantic? Most people guess satellites. In fact about 99% of data between continents travels through cables on the seabed.

beats.object: the Earth over the North Atlantic
beats.action: turns slowly as a dot pulses on London
launches from London and lands on New York
a number counts up on the mid-Atlantic

pages.section: Intuition: a cable as thick as a garden hose, carrying light
pages.say: Each cable is about as thick as a garden hose. Inside, hair-thin glass fibres carry pulses of light. One such line runs from the beach at Bude in Cornwall to the coast near New York.

beats.action: the camera flies down and tilts toward the beach at Bude
unrolls from Bude out into the North Atlantic
race along the route toward New York

pages.section: Mechanism: a web of about 550 cables wraps the planet
pages.say: That is one cable of roughly 550. Laid end to end they stretch about 1.4 million kilometres along the ocean floor. Together they tie every inhabited continent into one network.

beats.action: pulls back while cable routes light up across the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans
a number counts up on the open ocean as routes keep unrolling
pulse one after another as the routes reach them

pages.section: Landing points: the cables come ashore at a handful of beaches
pages.say: All those cables come ashore at a small number of places. Cornwall in England, Marseille in France, Mumbai in India and Singapore are among the busiest. Singapore alone is a meeting point for cables from across Asia.

beats.action: dots pulse on each landing point in turn
the camera flies east and Singapore lights up
fan out from Singapore to Hong Kong, Tokyo, Sydney and Mumbai

pages.section: The turn: narrow passages and passing anchors
pages.say: Many routes between Europe and Asia squeeze through the Red Sea and past Egypt. Most cable breaks are caused by ship anchors and fishing gear. Special repair ships then haul the cable up and splice it back together.

beats.action: glows red as several routes bunch together through it
highlights where the routes cross land toward the Mediterranean
flickers off at a break point, then relights

pages.section: Close: the world's conversations ride on light under the sea
pages.say: So the next time you call someone abroad, picture your words as light running along the seabed. About 99% of data between continents makes that trip.

beats.action: pulls back to a full view as every route of the film lights at once
keep flowing as the final number lands on the ocean
